newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable in slow late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable in slow late trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in late trading on Friday, dealers said.
They said trading was dull, with operators seen shrugging off the Thursday riots in the west Java town of Tasikmalaya.
One Japanese bank dealer said operators were mainly staying on the sidelines amid excess rupiah supply in the money market.
"There is no drive in the market. People are just waiting for the day to pass. They don't want to take any initiative at this time of the year," the dealer said.
Dealers said the market would be even quieter on Monday, the year's last trading day.
The foreign exchange market will be closed on December 31 and January 1, and reopens on January 2.
Spot rupiah was at 2,363.3/63.5 at 0900 GMT against an opening of 2,362.0/63.0. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,363.10/63.35 and 2,362.25/62.50, respectively.
The rupiah was briefly jolted in the morning due to news of the riots, but it managed to recover quickly to the opening level from the day's low of 2,364.5 on local support.
They said the Tasikmalaya riots were unlike riots in the past, when operators responded swiftly with rupiah selling.
One foreign bank dealer said the absence of offshore operators due to the holiday season helped prevent any drastic response in the foreign exchange market.
He said reaction was brief because the riots did not spread to other places.
Residents of Tasikmalaya said a crowd of several thousand people ran amok apparently after police had allegedly beaten religious school teachers.
They said the mob set fire to churches, shops, commercial buildings and vehicles. A military official said at least two people had died in the rioting.
Hundreds of troops patrolled the riot-torn town on Friday.
Dealers said sentiment on the rupiah remained firm, with many operators still watching the central bank band.
They said swap rates remained soft on ample liquidity.
Overnight swap was at 0.2/0.3 and tom/next at 0.4/0.5.
One-month swaps was at 14.00/14.25, two at 28.00/29.00, three at 41.1/42.5 and six at 84.50/86.50 points.
Bank Indonesia kept its intervention rate at 2,358/2,550 and the conversion rate to 2,358/2,406 on Friday.
